reviews.text: I have three cats and have been taking them to Dr. Calderara for five years. He's a very empathetic and kind vet; he saved Ronnie from invasive surgery, and he's extremely fair about his pricing. Thank you, Doc 🙏
Friendliness, punctuality, and love for animals. The doctor is very professional and available both to explain and to help our puppies.

Unfortunately, I lost my longtime vet, whom I was very fond of. Thanks to a friend's recommendation, I think I've found exactly what I was looking for. Professional and honest. 5 stars, well deserved.

Kindness, honesty, and friendliness on canvas: a true professional! Even after two necessary and successful procedures, my cat still trusts him without complaint, and so do I.
Attentive, helpful, competent, and honest professional! He treats animals with care and attention.
I have known Angelo for 20 years since 2007 first with my Angel and now with Zoe and Bizè unique with true love towards our furry friends and incredible honesty and I will never change him again

We said our final farewell to our dog, after 16 years of life together, at Dr. Calderara's office, and we can never thank him enough for the kindness and care he showed us during such a painful time.
He is an empathetic professional, capable of understanding the pain a family is experiencing. It's clear how much he loves animals and cares for their well-being, right up to the last moment.
We thank him from the bottom of our hearts for the humanity, respect, and kindness he showed us.

The Dr. Calderara, in my opinion, is one of the few veterinarians in Milan who do not speculate on the health of our animals.
Their health takes priority over his profit.
Honest, competent, friendly, very empathetic.
Of a rare humanity.
Highly recommended.

Incompetent Veterinarian.
I took my 9-month-old dog for a previous case of vaginitis. She'd already been on antibiotics with another vet and had an ultrasound to check for damage to her uterus.
He, as if nothing had happened, gave her the antibiotic without doing an ultrasound or checking her.
That evening we took her to the clinic, they had an ultrasound done on my dog, and guess what? She has pyometra, meaning her uterus has been damaged. They operated on her this morning, and we're picking her up this afternoon.
I wouldn't recommend this vet; he was truly superficial, and he could have killed my dog.

It's a real shame that we only met him during our dog's final days, but we couldn't have asked for a better professional and person at that time. Our little girl obviously didn't like vets, but she immediately felt at ease with him, which is extremely rare. He treated her with a kindness and love I rarely see from a vet, and he was honest and sincere with us right to the end. Thank you so much for your compassion.
